subject: Polity
description: Council of States: composition, election, term, special powers

questions.stem: MAXIMUM strength of Rajya Sabha as per the Constitution is:

options.option_text: 238 elected members maximum
250 (238 elected + 12 nominated)
245 elected only members allowed
543 same as Lok Sabha total

questions.explanation: RAJYA SABHA (Council of States; UPPER HOUSE; permanent body) — Article 80. MAX strength = 250: 238 from STATES + UTs (elected by state MLAs) + 12 NOMINATED by President (for distinguished service in literature, science, art, social service). Currently ~245 actual (some seats vacant; Anglo-Indian provision earlier removed). Term = 6 YEARS for each member; 1/3 retire every 2 YEARS (PERMANENT body, never dissolved). India is in Parliament's 18th LS but RS is continuous.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: MEMBERS of Rajya Sabha from STATES are elected by:

options.option_text: Citizens directly by an adult-suffrage vote
Members of state legislative assemblies (MLAs)
Lok Sabha members from that particular state
Council of Ministers of the state cabinet only

questions.explanation: RS members from STATES — INDIRECTLY elected by elected MEMBERS of the STATE LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLIES (MLAs); SINGLE TRANSFERABLE VOTE (proportional representation). NOT by general public. Note: Anti-defection law (10th Schedule) doesn't restrict cross-voting in RS elections (post 2003 amendment) — leads to horse-trading sometimes. RS members from UTs (Delhi, Puducherry only) — also indirectly elected. Other UTs (J&K + Ladakh, A&N, Chandigarh etc.) don't have RS representation. CHAIRMAN of RS = Vice President (ex-officio).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: TERM of a Rajya Sabha member is:

options.option_text: 5 years (same as Lok Sabha) here
6 years (with 1/3 retiring every 2 yrs)
4 years (less than Lok Sabha) here
Until age of 65 only allowed in office

questions.explanation: Term of RS member = 6 YEARS. STAGGERED election: 1/3 of members RETIRE every 2 YEARS → continuous House, never dissolved. Compare LS = 5 years (or until dissolved). RS = 'PERMANENT BODY' (Article 83 — RS shall NOT be subject to dissolution). RS gives stability + continuity; LS reflects current popular will. Min age: 30 years (vs 25 for LS); citizen of India; not in office of profit; etc.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Rajya Sabha has SPECIAL POWERS exclusive to it under Articles 249 + 312:

options.option_text: Can pass Money Bills alone without LS approval
Can authorise Parliament on State List + create AIS
Can dissolve the Lok Sabha at will any time
Can impeach the President alone without LS

questions.explanation: Two SPECIAL POWERS of Rajya Sabha (only RS, not LS): (1) Article 249 — RS can pass resolution by 2/3 majority enabling Parliament to LEGISLATE on a STATE LIST subject in NATIONAL INTEREST (max 1 year, renewable). Used rarely. (2) Article 312 — RS can authorise creation of NEW ALL-INDIA SERVICES (in addition to IAS, IPS, IFoS) by 2/3 majority. New services = Indian Engineering Service, Indian Forest Service (added 1966), Indian Medical Service etc. — proposals via this route. RATIONALE: federalism — RS represents STATE interests, so any encroachment on state powers needs RS's go-ahead.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: On a MONEY BILL, the Rajya Sabha can:

options.option_text: Reject it outright with no consequence
Only RECOMMEND changes within 14 days
Pass it into law without LS approval
Demand a joint sitting on the bill

questions.explanation: Money Bill (Art 110): can ONLY be introduced in LS (with President's recommendation). After LS passes, sent to RS — RS has 14 DAYS to RECOMMEND changes. LS can ACCEPT or REJECT recommendations. After 14 days (or LS rejection), bill is DEEMED PASSED. RS effectively has no veto on Money Bills — design choice to keep financial control with the directly elected House. JOINT SITTING is NOT used for money bills. Speaker decides whether bill is a Money Bill — final decision (Article 110(3)).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Some famous NOMINATED members of Rajya Sabha have included:

options.option_text: Rahul Gandhi (he was only an LS MP from UP)
Lata, Tendulkar, Rekha, Swaminathan as nominees
Modi, Manmohan, Vajpayee (the past PMs only)
Only retired bureaucrats and ex-judges allowed

questions.explanation: Article 80(3) — President nominates 12 members from those distinguished in: literature, science, art, SOCIAL SERVICE. Notable nominees: SACHIN TENDULKAR (cricket, 2012-18); LATA MANGESHKAR (singer, 1999-2005); REKHA (actress, 2012-18); MS SWAMINATHAN (Green Revolution scientist); JAVED AKHTAR (lyricist); SHABANA AZMI; AMRITA PRITAM (poet); SATYAJIT RAY (filmmaker); ALVA, NARGIS (actress); recent: P.T. USHA (sports), Ilaiyaraja (musician). Note Manmohan Singh (was PM but RS member, not nominated — elected from Assam).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: DEPUTY CHAIRMAN of Rajya Sabha is elected by:

options.option_text: President (presidential nomination)
Members of Rajya Sabha among themselves
Both Houses jointly in joint sitting
Vice President as RS Chairman alone

questions.explanation: Article 89 — DEPUTY CHAIRMAN of RS — elected by members of RS amongst themselves. Removed by RESOLUTION passed by majority of all then members of RS (with 14-day notice). Presides when CHAIRMAN (= Vice President) is absent. PANEL OF VICE-CHAIRMEN — additional members nominated by Chairman to preside in absence of both Chair + Deputy. For LS: SPEAKER + DEPUTY SPEAKER (both elected by LS members from amongst themselves). Speaker of LS presides over JOINT SITTINGS.
